usual_baseline: Risk assessment on admission is usually done (93–100%) [1390][1702][2717]. The weak items are lying and standing BP, 25–34% [1610][1702][1903], and medication review after a fall, 9.09% [1817] and 22% [1761]. Call bell in reach 56% [1823]. Nationally, flat lifting equipment used in 22% [1169].
fix_that_works: Prompts built into routine. Education, SystmOne prompts and weekly MDT fall reviews: medication review 22% to 94% [1761]. Teaching, posters and aide-memoires: LSBP 32% to 83.3% [1610]. Huddle reminders and flyers: LSBP 34% to 68% [1702]. Stickers, teaching and handover reminders: call bell in reach 56% to 93.88% [1823]. Checklist and education: composite 65% to 90% [1903].
fix_that_fails: Continuous national audit moved slowly: flat lifting 22% to 29%, medical assessment within 30 minutes 52% to 60% [1169]. LSBP stayed at 65% after a checklist [1903]. LSBP was sometimes ticked as done when it was not [1702]. The call bell project showed no link with falls [1823].
consultant_advice: Lying and standing BP has been done often with the same result. More useful: audit medication review and deprescribing after a fall, which was 9.09% in one hospital [1817], or post-fall management such as CT head criteria [1171]. Measure falls or harm, not just process.
